rows.sentence: The notes stop students guessing in the dark.
rows.guideMeaning: Trying to answer without enough information; a fixed darkness metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaningEn: Try to understand, answer or proceed without enough information, examples or guidance.
rows.targetPattern: \bgrop(?:e|es|ed|ing) in the dark\b|\bguess(?:es|ed|ing)? in the dark\b

rows.sentence: The device gathered dust once the novelty wears off.
rows.guideMeaning: The excitement of newness fades; a fixed clothing metaphor.
rows.ownerMeaningEn: The initial excitement, novelty or attraction fades after someone becomes familiar with the experience, object or its difficulties.
rows.targetPattern: \bthe shine (?:soon )?(?:wears|wore|can wear|has worn) off\b|\bthe novelty (?:wears|wore|can wear|has worn) off\b

rows.expression: get its foot in the door
rows.sentence: A catchy advert may get its foot in the door.
rows.guideMeaning: Gain an initial chance to influence someone; a fixed foot idiom.
rows.ownerMeaningEn: An initial opportunity to enter a field, organisation or activity, or to gain someone’s attention, without guaranteeing a lasting position or influence.

sourceGrammarNote3703: The exact guide sentence mixes gathered (past) with wears (present); provenance is verbatim, while the owner grammar and takeaway model the aligned past wore off. This source weakness remains visible for independent editorial judgment.
materialLimits: Phrase detectors are lexical; context must still distinguish literal darkness, physical shine, and an actual foot/door from figurative use.
Advert its foot in the door is a personified extension of an initial chance to influence, not a guarantee of purchase.
release: unpublished; no listening or deployment claim
